_about: The phase-in of scope 3 emissions that Pillar 3 ESG Template 1 column j points to, quoted from the stored texts (every quote checked word for word by tests/unit/test_t1_financed_emissions.py). Annex XL, Template 1, column j (Implementing Regulation (EU) 2022/2453, CELEX 32022R2453): see 'basis'. Article 5(1) of Delegated Regulation (EU) 2020/1818 (CELEX 32020R1818) phases scope 3 in by NACE division (Annex I to Regulation (EC) No 1893/2006) and date. Dates are computed by services.governance.pillar3_t1 from the anchor date and the years each point names; nothing here is a typed date except the quoted anchor. Read by services/governance/pillar3_t1.py.

basis.quote: Institutions shall disclose their scope 3 emissions on a best effort basis, covering the most relevant sectors in line with PCAF approach and the phased-in approach for scope 3 emissions included in Article 5 of Delegated Regulation (EU) 2020/1818.
Institutions shall disclose information on scope 3 emissions of the counterparty for all sectors included in the template with first reference date as of 30 June 2024.

article.quote: The benchmark methodology for EU Climate Transition Benchmarks or EU Paris-aligned Benchmarks shall include Scope 3 GHG emissions data in the following way:

period_rules.quote: Save as otherwise provided, this Regulation shall apply to acts of the Council or Commission which have been or will be passed pursuant to the Treaty establishing the European Economic Community or the Treaty establishing the European Atomic Energy Community.

Where a period expressed in days, weeks, months or years is to be calculated from the moment at which an event occurs or an action takes place, the day during which that event occurs or that action takes place shall not be considered as falling within the period in question.

(c) a period expressed in weeks, months or years shall start at the beginning of the first hour of the first day of the period, and shall end with the expiry of the last hour of whichever day in the last week, month or year is the same day of the week, or falls on the same date, as the day from which the period runs.
Where the last day of a period expressed otherwise than in hours is a public holiday, Sunday or Saturday, the period shall end with the expiry of the last hour of the following working day.

points.quote: (a) As of 23 December 2020, Scope 3 GHG emissions data for at least the energy and mining sectors referred to in Divisions 05 to 09 and 19 and 20 of Annex I to Regulation (EC) No 1893/2006;

(b) within two years from 23 December 2020, Scope 3 GHG emissions data for at least the transportation, construction, buildings, materials and industrial sectors referred to in Divisions 10 to 18, 21 to 33, 41, 42 and 43, 49 to 53 and Division 81 of Annex I to Regulation (EC) No 1893/2006;
(c) within four years from 23 December 2020, Scope 3 GHG emissions data for all other sectors referred to in Annex I to Regulation (EC) No 1893/2006.

interpretations.reading: Article 5 of Delegated Regulation (EU) 2020/1818 is addressed to administrators of EU Climate Transition and Paris-aligned Benchmarks; Annex XL points Template 1 column j to it ('in line with ... the phased-in approach for scope 3 emissions included in Article 5'). It is read as a calendar per NACE division: for a disclosure reference date, a division is phased in once the date of its point has been reached, and before that it is in its phase-in period. Nothing is removed from column j for a division in its phase-in period — the points say 'at least'; it is shown as such.
interpretations.why: The ITS names the article but does not restate it; the benchmark regulation is the only text of the phase-in.

interpretations.reading: Regulation (EEC, Euratom) No 1182/71 on periods, dates and time limits ('period_rules') applies to Delegated Regulation (EU) 2020/1818, a Commission act adopted under the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union, the successor of the Treaty its Article 1 names. By its Article 3(1) and 3(2)(c) (quoted), 'within two years from 23 December 2020' and 'within four years from 23 December 2020' end with the expiry of 23 December 2022 and 23 December 2024; a disclosure reference date is the state at the end of its day, so a division of point (b) or (c) is phased in for a reference date on or after that day. Neither day is a Saturday or Sunday (Article 3(4)); whether it is a public holiday where the institution acts (Article 2(1)) is not held.
interpretations.why: The period's last day is computed by the quoted rules; that those rules reach a TFEU-era act is the reading declared here.

interpretations.reading: For a reference date on or after 30 June 2024 the ITS itself requires scope 3 'for all sectors included in the template', whatever a division's Article 5 status; both are shown side by side.
interpretations.why: Annex XL, column j, quoted in 'basis'.
